title: Clause processing preserves the canonical path
statement: Fix $n$, a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables, and two restrictions $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ on those variables. Suppose $t$ is the first term of $f$ not killed by $\rho_0$, that $t$ has no repeated literal, and that any two literals of $t$ with equal variables are themselves equal. Let $\mathrm{lits}$ be the list of literals of $t$ whose variable is free under $\rho_0$, each tagged with its position in $t$, and let $\mathrm{path}$ be a canonical path for $f|_{\rho_0}$ — an initial segment of the deepest root-to-leaf path of the canonical decision tree of $f|_{\rho_0}$ — of length at most the depth of the canonical decision tree of $f|_{\rho_0}$. Assume that for every index $k$ below the smaller of the lengths of $\mathrm{lits}$ and $\mathrm{path}$, the variable of the $k$-th literal of $\mathrm{lits}$ equals the variable queried at the $k$-th step of $\mathrm{path}$. Process $\mathrm{lits}$ against $\mathrm{path}$ in lockstep, one path step per literal, forming a restriction $\rho_0'$ and a shortened path $\mathrm{path}'$ as follows: a literal with variable $v$ and negation flag $b$ aligned with a path step of direction $d$ contributes the assignment $v \mapsto d$ to $\rho_0'$ (and the assignment $v \mapsto \lnot b$ to $\sigma$), and its path step is dropped; $\rho_0'$ agrees with $\rho_0$ on every other variable, and $\mathrm{path}'$ is the unconsumed tail of $\mathrm{path}$. Then $\mathrm{path}'$ is a canonical path for $f|_{\rho_0'}$, and the length of $\mathrm{path}'$ is at most the depth of the canonical decision tree of $f|_{\rho_0'}$.
